tagline: Up Highway 9 through the cotton valleys to a mountaintop river.
intro: From I-20 near Heflin the byway runs west with US 78 through the Talladega National Forest, then turns north on Highway 9 by White Plains and the Dugger Mountain Scenic Drive. Past Piedmont and Ellisville it goes through cotton fields to Centre, which took the county seat in 1844 for being central and was named for it, in the British spelling.

From Leesburg, Highway 273 runs northeast past plantations and cotton fields in deep mountain valleys. At Blanche the road turns onto Highway 35, climbs Lookout Mountain, crosses the Little River Canyon preserve and comes down into Fort Payne, about 80 miles from where it started.

moments.title: Piedmont
moments.text: First called Hollow Stump, then Cross Plains, and Piedmont only from 1888, the town got its railroad in 1868, and the old depot now holds a museum.

moments.title: Little River Canyon
moments.text: A river that runs almost its whole length along the top of Lookout Mountain, between sandstone cliffs up to 600 feet high.

moments.title: Fort Payne
moments.text: A late-1880s boom town whose iron and coal proved smaller than expected, it did better with socks, and around 2000 its mills made more than half the socks produced in the United States.
